land.text: Selangor under a British Resident: Sultan Abdul Samad asked Andrew Clarke in October 1875 to make Selangor a British protectorate and James Guthrie Davidson, 'the first British resident in Selangor', was soon appointed

successors.note: A protectorate, not an annexation: the sultanate continues (the page's rulers table runs on to the present). Cliopatria ends its row in 1876; the pages opened give October 1875 for the request and no year for the Resident's appointment.

capitals.name: Kuala Selangor (Kota Malawati)
capitals.note: The page: Kota Malawati at Kuala Selangor was 'the residence of the three earliest Sultan'; it gives no years, so the span is the three reigns of its rulers table (Salehuddin, Ibrahim, Muhammad Shah, to 1857). Dutch attack of 1784 drove Sultan Ibrahim out of the fort for under a year. Coordinates approximate (the page gives none).

capitals.name: Jugra
capitals.note: Istana Jugra 'built in 1876' was Abdul Samad's residence (page). The page names no seat for 1858-1875, so the capital list has a gap there; coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Salehuddin (Raja Lumu)
rulers.note: The rulers table starts his reign in 1743; the text has him installed as first Sultan by Sultan Mahmud Shah in November 1766.

rulers.name: Abdul Samad
rulers.note: Reigned beyond the dossier's end (1876) as a British-protected sultan.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria 1744 outline, one year earlier: the infobox gives the formation as 1743, when Raja Lumu was made Yamtuan Selangor

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's first Selangor shape starts in 1744; the page's infobox formation is 1743 ('appointed his son, Raja Lumu to become Yamtuan Selangor on 1743'). The page also has the installation as Sultan in November 1766, which the ledger records as a rename.

11,824 km2, 31 grid cells, bbox 100.75-102.10E, 2.54-3.89N: the Selangor of the page (Kuala Selangor, Klang, Langat valleys). The page gives no area; the gazetteer's admin-1 Selangor is 23 cells and Kuala Lumpur is separate, so the shape is the modern state plus the capital territory and a coastal margin. Johor claimed overlordship ('assumed Selangor is still a part of his territory', February 1756) without changing the outline.

11,709 km2 against 11,824 km2 before. At the grid's resolution (H3 res 5) the 1744, 1775 and 1873 outlines are the same 31 cells, so the 115 km2 shift on the Negeri Sembilan border is below what the map shows and no ledger event is written; the pages opened do not mention it. The 1826-1857 division of Selangor into five territories (Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Langat, Lukut, page) was internal and left the outline whole.

11,766 km2, the same 31 cells. The outline stands through the end of the war (fighting 'largely ended' 8 November 1873) and to 1876; the rebel-held towns of 1867-1873 are overlaid by the ledger's loss/gain events with the rebel faction raja-mahdi-s-faction.

region.text: Selangor: the page names Kota Malawati (Kuala Selangor) as the early seat and gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1743: Raja Lumu is made Yamtuan Selangor. Infobox formation 1743; 'appointed his son, Raja Lumu to become Yamtuan Selangor on 1743'; the Bugis dynasty 'descended from ... the rulers of Luwu'. Johor held that Selangor was still its territory (1756), so 'nobody' is the page-neutral counterpart.

November 1766: the Yamtuan becomes the first Sultan of Selangor. Raja Lumu was 'installed by Sultan Mahmud Shah as the first Sultan of Selangor in November 1766', as Salehuddin, after Perak's recognition; the rulers table dates his reign from 1743.

region.text: Kuala Selangor and the fort of Kota Malawati

ledger.note: 1784: the Dutch take Kuala Selangor. 'In 1784, he was defeated in the attack on Kuala Selangor by the Dutch', which forced Sultan Ibrahim out of Kota Malawati. The Dutch side is the VOC, filed under dutch-republic.

region.text: Kuala Selangor and the fort of Kota Malawati

ledger.note: 1785 (or late 1784): Ibrahim retakes the fort. The page says only that he retook it 'in less than a year with the help of the Pahang Kingdom'; 1785 is the researcher's bridging year.

region.text: the fort and town of Klang

ledger.note: March 1867: Raja Mahdi seizes Klang. 'In March 1867, Raja Mahdi captured the fort of Klang'; Raja Abdullah had already left for Malacca. The dispute began in 1866 over opium taxes in the Klang Valley.

region.text: Klang, retaken by Raja Ismail and Tengku Kudin

ledger.note: March 1870: Klang is retaken. 'In March 1870, Raja Ismail, assisted by Tengku Kudin, laid siege to Klang City'; Mahdi withdrew north, and the page has Kudin holding Klang from 1870.

region.text: Kuala Selangor, Raja Mahdi's stronghold from 1870

ledger.note: March 1870: Mahdi falls back on Kuala Selangor. The page: Mahdi 'withdrew north to Kuala Selangor' and held it 1870-1871; the month is that of the Klang siege.
July 1871: Kuala Selangor is taken from Mahdi. After a pirate attack was traced to 'Raja Mahdi's stronghold in Kuala Selangor', the British captured the town and gave it to Kudin.
1872: Mahdi takes Kuala Lumpur. The page: Mahdi took Kuala Lumpur and it was razed.
1872: Kuala Selangor falls to Mahdi's forces again, after Kuala Lumpur.
March 1873: Kuala Lumpur is retaken. 'In March 1873, Kudin's men, supported by Pahangese fighters, defeated Syed Mashhor in Kuala Lumpur.'
8 November 1873: Kuala Selangor falls to Pahang and Kudin. 'on 8 November 1873 the Pahangese forces captured Kuala Selangor'; fighting 'largely ended' and Mahdi went into exile in 1874.

1876: Selangor passes under a British Resident. Page: 'In October 1875, Sultan Abdul Samad asked Andrew Clarke to make Selangor a British protectorate'; Davidson was 'soon appointed' first Resident, no year given. 1876 is Cliopatria's last year for the row and the researcher's bridge; the sultanate itself continued.

wars.name: Selangor Civil War

zones.text: Klang, held by Mahdi March 1867 to March 1870
Kuala Selangor, held by Mahdi 1870-July 1871 and 1872-8 November 1873
Kuala Lumpur, held by Mahdi 1872 to March 1873

wars.outcome: Tengku Kudin and Raja Ismail, with Pahangese forces and British help, drove Raja Mahdi from Klang (1870), Kuala Selangor (July 1871; again 8 November 1873) and Kuala Lumpur (March 1873); Mahdi went into exile in 1874. The war ended Britain's non-intervention: the page has the Pangkor Agreement of 1874 and Selangor's request for a protectorate in October 1875.
wars.note: The article says the conflict 'lasted from 1866 to 1874'. Perak was not a belligerent (Syed Mashhor took refuge there).

wars.name: Dutch attack on Kuala Selangor (1784)

zones.text: Kuala Selangor and the fort of Kota Malawati

wars.outcome: The Dutch defeated Sultan Ibrahim at Kuala Selangor in 1784 and forced him out of Kota Malawati; he retook the fort in under a year with help from Pahang.
wars.note: The war has no article title on the page; the name is descriptive. The end year is the researcher's bridge for 'less than a year'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by the pages opened: the realm is a set of river-valley principalities (Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Langat, Lukut) with approximate frontiers, and the Pangkor-era treaties fix none of them.

sources.title: Selangor Sultanate (Sultan of Selangor)
sources.note: Identity, 1743 and 1766 dates, Kota Malawati, the 1784 Dutch attack, the five territories, rulers, no area given.

sources.title: Selangor Civil War
sources.note: Dated campaigns of 1867-1873 for Klang, Kuala Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, British involvement, the 1875 request for a protectorate.

notes: Page budget: two pages (Sultan of Selangor, Selangor Civil War). Neither gives an area or the Federated Malay States (1896), so the end year 1876 follows Cliopatria and rests on the October 1875 request plus 'soon appointed' (confidence 1). The Cliopatria outline does not change at the grid's resolution in 1744, 1775 or 1873. Disagreement inside the first page: the infobox and rulers table date the first reign from 1743, the text has the installation as Sultan in November 1766; the dossier starts 1743 and records 1766 as a rename. Johor's claim ('assumed Selangor is still a part of his territory', February 1756; a treaty dated 8 January 1758 in the rulers table) is Johor's overlordship to record, not a territory change here; the 1744 'dutch-republic' neighbour in the seed is Malacca. Rebel overlay: Raja Mahdi held Klang for three years, so this dossier pairs with a rebel dossier raja-mahdi-s-faction written by the same batch. The civil-war page calls 'Selangor' the camp of the Sultan, Tengku Kudin and Raja Ismail; Raja Abdullah (Klang until Mahdi took it) is on the same side. Gazetteer names needed: Kuala Selangor (place; the radius disc uses lon 101.249, lat 3.344), Jugra, Kota Malawati. Capital coordinates are approximate. Capital gap 1858-1875: the page names no seat.
